title: Coordinate junta approximation
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. For real numbers $\epsilon,\eta>0$ and an integer $k\ge0$, suppose its total influence is positive and the sum of its squared Fourier coefficients over sets of size greater than $k$ is at most $\epsilon$. Set $\rho=\eta/(2+\eta)$ and $\tau=\bigl((\epsilon/I(f))\rho^k\bigr)^{1+\eta}$. Let $J$ consist of the coordinates whose pivotal probability is at least $\tau$, and let $g(x)$ be the sign of the conditional average of $f$ when the coordinates in $J$ are fixed to $x|_J$ and the other coordinates are uniform and independent (choosing $+1$ when that average is zero). Then the fraction of inputs on which $f$ and $g$ differ is at most $\epsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube to the signs
The total influence of $f$ is positive
The Fourier weight on sets of size greater than $k$ is at most $\epsilon$
